review.reason: 리뷰 거절: internal/proxy/tracking.go:231-248 handleMomentoProxy builds a fresh *http.Transport (and ReverseProxy) for every /momento/* request. A Transport keeps its keep-alive connection plus readLoop/writeLoop goroutines alive until the peer closes it (IdleConnTimeout is 0 on a custom Transport and CloseIdleConnections is never called), so every tracker.js fetch and every visitor beacon leaks one TCP connection to the collector and ~3 goroutines. Reproduced outside the repo with the identical pattern: 200 proxied requests -> goroutines 4 -> 604 after GC, none reclaimed. Under real visitor traffic this is an unbounded fd/goroutine leak on the success path. Fix: one shared Transport on the Server (or at least DisableKeepAlives/CloseIdleConnections). The proxy integration test (TestMomentoProxyForwardsSameOriginTraffic) cannot catch this because it makes only two requests. / internal/proxy/tracking.go:91 tracking.allowed_hosts is registered with no validator, and SplitHosts (internal/tracking/tracking.go:248-260) only splits on comma/whitespace, so whatever an operator types via PUT /admin/settings/by-key/tracking.allowed_hosts is spliced verbatim into script-src/connect-src/img-src (tracking.go:240-242, policy.go:54). Values such as 'unsafe-inline', *, data:, or https://a.example;default-src * pass straight into the Content-Security-Policy header of every /app page. This contradicts the commit message, the package doc (tracking.go:10), and ADMIN_GUIDE.md 3.6 ('never unsafe-inline' / 'widened by exactly those origins'). The /admin/tracking/violations/allow path validates strictly (tracking.go:313-318) but the ordinary settings write does not, so the documented invariant is unenforced on the path the runtime-settings tab actually uses.
